name: Gschnitz
kurzbeschreibung: Charming mountain village in the Wipptal – the gateway to the enchanting Gschnitztal, home to the mountain lake and the ruins of Gschnitzer Burg.
beschreibung:
Overview

Gschnitz is situated at an altitude of 1,242 metres at the head of the romantic Gschnitztal valley, a south-western branch of the Wipptal in the district of Innsbruck-Land. Located roughly 35 kilometres south of the provincial capital Innsbruck, the municipality covers almost 75 square kilometres and is home to around 450 residents. The tranquil high-mountain valley is enclosed by the majestic peaks of the Stubai Alps and the Tribulaun group, traversed by the pristine waters of the Gschnitzbach stream. Together with the neighbouring village of Trins, the valley holds the prestigious designation of an official Mountaineering Village (Bergsteigerdorf) awarded by the Alpine Clubs. Here, authentic natural beauty, traditional mountain farming, pristine forests, and quiet alpine serenity prevail over mass commercial tourism.

History

The historical settlement of this alpine valley traces back to early medieval Bavarian colonization, while the name Gschnitz derives from the Celtic word cassaniciu, translating roughly as place near the oaks. The settlement was first documented in 1288 in the Tyrolean land register of Count Meinhard II as Gasnitz. The backbone of early life was formed by exactly nine sovereign pastoral farms known as Schwaighöfe, seven located in the valley basin and two on the high alpine Laponesalm pasture. In enduring tribute to these founding farms, nine gabled roofs adorn the official municipal coat of arms. High above the valley perches the pilgrimage chapel of St. Magdalena, first mentioned in records in 1307 and housing some of North Tyrol's oldest Romanesque frescoes. In the village centre, the parish church of Our Lady of the Snows was sumptuously redesigned in Rococo style between 1755 and 1759 by renowned priest-architect Franz de Paula Penz.

Getting There

By automobile, travel from the north via the Brenner Motorway A13 to the exit for Matrei am Brenner or Steinach am Brenner. From there, follow the Brenner Road B182 briefly towards the valley and turn onto the provincial road L10 into the Gschnitztal valley, which leads straight into the village after approximately 15 kilometres. Train travellers can take the ÖBB Brenner Railway or Tyrol S-Bahn line S3 from Innsbruck Central Station to Steinach am Brenner station. Directly at the station forecourt, connecting VVT regional bus line 4145 provides seamless public transport into Gschnitz and out to the terminus near Alpengasthof Feuerstein.

Tips

A natural highlight is the thunderous Sandes Waterfall at the valley head, cascading down rugged rocky cliffs. Close by, the Mühlendorf Gschnitz open-air museum brings historical craft traditions, water-driven grain mills, and a forge to life. For hikers and mountaineers, Gschnitz is an outstanding gateway: Classic alpine trekking routes lead up to Innsbrucker Hütte beneath the imposing Habicht peak, to Bremer Hütte, or to the family-friendly Laponesalm. In winter, the valley floor transforms into a cross-country skiing haven, offering over 18 kilometres of groomed trails through pristine snowy landscapes.
